title: Settlement Agreements Schedule of Due-Date Extension Allowances and Fulfillment Hold Periods
content:
# Settlement Agreements — Extension Allowances and Fulfillment Hold

Three programme figures of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements govern the later life of an accepted settlement: how many due-date extensions one accepted settlement may receive, the largest number of calendar days one extension may add, and the business days after the final settlement payment is received before the settlement is treated as fulfilled.

| Figure | Prompt-Pay Discount Settlement | Lump-Sum Settlement | Two-Payment Settlement | Three-Payment Settlement | Six-Payment Settlement | Hardship Settlement |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Due-date extensions allowed per accepted settlement | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| Largest number of calendar days one extension may add | 0 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 15 | 15 |
| Fulfillment hold after the final payment is received (business days) | 5 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 |

## Notes

- The Prompt-Pay Discount Settlement allows no due-date extension: both its extension figures are 0.
- The extension maximum is the programme's ceiling for a single extension; the count is the number of extensions one accepted settlement may receive over its life.
- Business days for the fulfillment hold are Monday through Friday, excluding US federal legal public holidays.

## Hypothetical comparison

A hypothetical accepted Six-Payment Settlement may receive two extensions of up to 15 calendar days each; a hypothetical accepted Lump-Sum Settlement may receive one extension of up to 10 calendar days.
